findings.title: Do not accept view scope for group management
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE, so an administrator granted only view permission on all groups passes requireManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses that check to authorize both creating groups and moving existing subgroups to the top level. This gives a read-only administrator write access to the group hierarchy. Require only MANAGE here and add a negative test for group creation with only VIEW.

findings.title: Return model group IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
findings.body: This enumeration confuses authorization resources with group models. AdminPermissionsSchema creates individual resources with the group ID as their name, not their resource ID, and does not set their type to Groups. Consequently findByType does not enumerate those individual groups. For an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant, it instead finds the synthetic Groups resource and adds its authorization resource ID to the result. UsersResource uses this set as the group-membership filter for user searches and counts, so the all-groups grant produces a filter matching no actual group and hides all members. Individual group grants also fail to supply the IDs needed for counts and pre-pagination filtering. Resolve actual group IDs, evaluate individual resources using their names, and handle the synthetic all-groups resource explicitly; cover both individual and all-groups member searches and counts in tests.
